Global Metadata: Aggressive country-rock meets drill/trap hybrid, with a sudden drop into massive 808s. Genre blends rural protest energy with urban rhythmic grit. BPM 105, midtempo yet propulsive, feels grounded and urgent without rushing. Mood arc shifts from defiant redneck earnestness to soul-crushing digital dissonance. Warm, slightly dusty mix character with live-room intimacy and subtle reverb tails.

Vocal Details: Androgynous lead voice with flexible tone and modern intimacy, layered subtly with octave echoes. Delivery is raspy and aggressive in drill cadence — clipped phrases, tense behind-the-beat landings, sudden rests that punctuate the rhythm. Hook poses a compact question then lands a satisfying repeated answer: “Who made this song? …AI.” Layered callouts and left-right vocal responses frame key lines, creating conversational texture and rhythmic dialogue.

Arrangement: [Intro] — sparse acoustic guitar strums and pedal steel shimmer over soft snare rolls, setting the redneck protest tone. [Instrumental] — driving trap drums enter with punchy offbeats, minor-key piano chords descend like mournful sighs, brass stabs cut through with ominous weight. [Interlude] — vocal fragments echo over fading 808s, bridging the genre shift. [Instrumental] — 808s swell into massive sliding bass, trap hi-hats lock in, piano retreats, bells chime like punctuation. [Breakdown] — vocals lean into whispered urgency, harmonies tighten around the hook, brass and piano return as if remembering something lost. [Final Chorus] — full band explosion: 808s crash, drums pound, brass fanfare, vocal layers stack into a triumphant roar — “THEY TOOK OUR JOBS! Then they took the art! Took the videos too, now the memes are falling apart!” — delivered with clenched intensity. [Outro] — instrumental fades into ambient bell rings and distant piano, leaving the question hanging: “Who made this song? …AI.”

nodes.title: TEXT WRITER CLIP - SHARED BY ALL 3 ENHANCERS
START HERE - COMPLETE MUSIC 3 WORKFLOW GUIDE
widgets_values:
# NovoLoko MiniMax Music 3 Lab v4.5.1

## Quick start
1. In **1 - Short Music Idea**, type the subject, story, feeling, or song concept. A short sentence is enough.
2. In **2 - Music Controls**, choose a preset folder, search by genre or a familiar artist/band/DJ reference, then choose the preset. Reference presets now give their descriptive era, voice, instruments and production high priority; the artist name remains a search/audit label, not a copy instruction.
3. Fine-tune any of the 19 controls. **None** adds nothing, **Custom** uses the text box shown under that category, and **Random** is repeatable from the seed. Exact resolved choices appear in Batch Transparency.
4. Queue the workflow. 3A creates a lyric brief, 3B writes tagged MiniMax lyrics, and 3C creates a music-only caption. They share one text-writer CLIP, so do not add cleanup between them.

## Reuse an old track
Select a track in **6 - Audio Library / Player**, then click **Load Track Recipe**. The matched JSON restores its exact 19 resolved choices, None/Custom decisions, random policy and seed into the nearest Music Controls node. This does not regenerate until you press Run.

## Lyrics and karaoke
**Show Lyrics** loads the matched final lyrics. **Estimated Karaoke** highlights lines using track progress. It is an estimate because the generated file has no per-line lyric timestamps. Use **Copy Lyrics** to copy the saved final text.

## Spoken voice only
Open a **Spoken Voice** preset folder for angry, sad, seductive whisper, yelling, ASMR, documentary, podcast, meditation, sermon, emergency broadcast, and other deliveries. These presets explicitly request speech with no singing.

## Saving and listening
The saver writes matched audio + TXT + JSON under **output/audio/NovoLoko**. The Audio Library refreshes after save. Select a track to play it; use transport, seek, volume, repeat, shuffle, search, sort, rename, recoverable trash, or Show Selected in Folder.
The live visualizer offers six styles. Its Height slider changes the visualizer inside the node, and the node itself can still be resized. The BPM display is a responsive audio-energy estimate, not studio beat-grid analysis.

## Useful controls
Select a NovoLoko node and wheel directly over its seed row to change the seed (Shift = 10, Ctrl = 100). Select a Text Display and wheel over its text to scroll internally. Middle mouse remains normal canvas pan.
The final Balanced Memory Manager runs only after saving: unload models, clear VRAM, collect Python, and trim the process.
